messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout v2026.03.17.wave-2 in us-east-1 - health check fail rate 4.8% over 3m, 5xx spike detected. Auto-abort threshold configured at 3%. Not yet auto-aborted because traffic smoothing in progress.

alex_raft: saw the alert, joining. pinging oncall.

maya_r: oncall here, thanks alex. Can you paste the failing probe logs?

deploy-bot: failing probe sample: `HTTP/1.1 503` from instance i-0b3a45 (kvcache miss). 5xx concentrated on fastpath pods.

sre-lead: this looks like the new kernel/kvcache change in the canary. Start mitigations: 1) scale up canary pool by +20% 2) enable fallback variant (quantized->non-quant) 3) prepare rollback like we practiced.

alex_raft: scaling up now (autoscaler override). ETA ~30s.

oncall-bot: @pagerduty paging maya_r (high) and sre-lead (critical) — incident INC-20260317-001 created.

pagerduty: paged maya_r; awaiting ack.

maya_r: acked. I'm running health probe sweep and pulling traces. Any customer-facing 5xx reports?

engops: we have a spike in api-gateway error logs for a small set of tenants (~0.6% of traffic) showing timeouts then 502/503. No broad customer outage reported yet.

alex_raft: fallback variant is compatible, can flip with flag. Recommend flip + monitor for 5 minutes before rollback.

sre-lead: agree. Start flag flip to fallback-now. If 5xx remains above 2% for 5m, escalate to immediate rollback.

alex_raft: running flag command: ```
releasectl feature-flag set canary_fastpath=false --env=us-east-1 --wave=2
```

deploy-bot: feature flag change recorded by alex_raft. Propagating.

maya_r: seeing initial drop in 5xx within 60s to 2.1%. Continue monitoring.

sre-lead: monitoring window started. If we get sustaining >2% for next 4m, we hit abort criteria.

oncall-bot: (automated) health window 1m passed: 5xx now 1.8%. Keeping open.

engops: customers who hit error are in low-volume cohort; we've opened a support ticket with affected tenant IDs and notified CSMs. No broad pager escalation to oncall for Business yet.

alex_raft: good signal. I'm going to keep the canary wave paused and hold on full rollout. Schedule: keep hold for 30m, then re-evaluate with perf traces.

maya_r: agreed. I'll keep incident INC-20260317-001 open and will hand off to night oncall at 00:30PT if still open. Drafting short customer-facing summary: "We detected increased error rates for a new canary change in us-east-1. We immediately rolled back a fastpath flag and errors are now returning to baseline. We are monitoring and will follow up."

sre-lead: good. Add postmortem owner assignment: alex_raft and maya_r. Use runbook section: "canary-failure-live-mitigation" as checklist.

alex_raft: noted. I'll capture commands & timeline in the incident doc.

oncall-bot: handoff reminder set for 00:25PT. Tagging @engops for logs retention.

engops: retained detailed request traces and kvcache logs, pushed to incident bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20260317-001/

maya_r: closing operational actions for now — canary paused, fallback flag active, rollback not required. Will update if anything changes. :white_check_mark:

sre-lead: thanks all. If error creeps up again, we move to rollback: ```releasectl rollout abort --wave=2 --reason=\"canary 5xx\"``` and invoke full rollback playbook.

alex_raft: copy. incident doc link: https://intra.redwood/incident/INC-20260317-001 - I'm adding timeline and logs.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-20260317-001 status: MONITORING.

maya_r: handing off to night oncall @oncall-night at 00:30PT with summary above.

oncall-bot: handoff posted.

engops: if we need to revert flag globally: ```releasectl feature-flag set canary_fastpath=false --env=prod --all-regions``` — keep that as last-resort step.

sre-lead: excellent work. Postmortem assigned, will triage root cause and look for additional safeguards on canary kernel changes. :memo:
